top.title: Arsenal will only sell Gyokeres if this condition is met
top.description: Arsenal will only sell Gyokeres if this condition is met Viktor Gyokeres’ future at Arsenal remains uncertain as he continues to struggle to earn the confidence of manager Mikel Arteta and his teammates. The Swedish striker has yet to establish himself as the reliable attacking option the club expected when he arrived, raising questions about his long-term future at the Emirates Stadium. In midweek, Gyokeres produced a fantastic goal for Arsenal in the Champions League , demonstrating that he remains capable of moments of brilliance, as he regularly did during his time at Sporting Club. His performance offered a reminder of the quality he possesses and the contribution he can still make to the team. However, producing occasional moments of quality will not be enough to secure his position in the starting line-up. He needs to deliver consistently and demonstrate that he can be trusted to lead Arsenal’s attack. So far, that consistency has been missing from his performances. Arsenal consider their options over Gyokeres Gyokeres has struggled to demonstrate the consistency required to become Arsenal’s leading striker. Although the club could consider selling him if an attractive offer arrives, they are not prepared to sanction his departure without carefully considering their options. According to Football Insider , Arsenal would ideally like to secure a top replacement for the Swedish forward before agreeing to let him leave. The report suggests that the Gunners still consider him an important member of their squad and would therefore want to ensure they have another attacking option ready before approving a transfer. This approach indicates that Arsenal are not necessarily looking to force Gyokeres out of the club. Instead, they appear to be preparing for different possibilities while ensuring that their attacking options remain strong enough to compete. (Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images) Gyokeres’ future depends on Arsenal’s recruitment Gyokeres reportedly wants to remain at Arsenal, but his future is not entirely in his own hands. His performances over the coming period could influence the club’s thinking, although recruitment decisions will also play an important role. If Arsenal identify and secure a replacement capable of providing more goals, they could become more willing to consider offers for the Swede. top.title: Patriots defense preparing for every quarterback possibility with Chargers
top.description: The New England Patriots are not the only team facing quarterback questions heading into Week 12. The Los Angeles Chargers, their opponent on Sunday, are in the same boat. Starting QB Justin Herbert remains in concussion protocol and was a no-show at practice both Wednesday and Thursday. With his status in question, backup D.J. Uiagalelei might be elevated into the starting role. Given that uncertainty, the Patriots defense is faced with a question: who to prepare for? “That’s a question that gets asked a lot: ‘You don’t know if a quarterback’s going to play or not, do you prepare for all of them?’ It’s lot about us,” defensive coordinator Zak Kuhr explained earlier this week. “Obviously, we know a lot more about Herbert’s play style than the next two guys, D.J. and Jake [Browning], if they make Jake active. But they are aware of their play styles. Obviously, there’s a lot more tape of Herbert, but everybody’s aware of the contingency plans. We went over that again [Wednesday], the contingency plans if we get news if something else changes.” Kuhr likened the situation to preparing for Denver Broncos backup quarterback Jarrett Stidham ahead of last year’s AFC Championship Game. That contest came two weeks after New England’s most recent meeting with Herbert, whose offense was held to three points in the wild card round. Uiagalelei was inactive as a member of the Chargers’ practice squad that day. Now, 10 months later, he is in line to potentially get his first career start and add to a résumé consisting of a mere 21 regular season snaps — all of them in a loss to the Texans earlier this season — as well as two pass completions on seven attempts for 24 yards and a touchdown. Despite the limited output so far, the Patriots have to familiarize themselves with the 25-year-old former undrafted free agent. And in the process of doing so, they have seen some differences to Los Angeles’ regular starter. “Strong arm. I would say more from the pocket than Herbert,” Kuhr said about his game. “Obviously, some inexperience. But he made some plays in college; obviously, he’s made a roster. So, I would say he’s a professional, he’s going to take advantage of his opportunity just like every backup quarterback does.”

top.title: Dolphins counting on rookies to push through NFL's 'rookie wall'
top.description: MIAMI GARDENS — It's Week 12 in the NFL and Kadyn Proctor of the Miami Dolphins is one of the many rookies who played 12 regular-season college games last year. Now, Proctor had three more games because Alabama always plays extra games. But the point here is that all NFL rookies hit the proverbial "rookie wall" at some point in late November or December. "I feel wonderful," Proctor said this week. "I've been telling my teammates. They've informed me about the rookie wall. I said I'm not going to hit it." The Dolphins (1-9) host the Jets (3-8) on Sunday, Nov. 29 at Hard Rock Stadium. And no team in the NFL has relied more on rookies than the Dolphins this season. "The wall's a concern for a big part of our team that are rookies and that are playing a lot of snaps, right?" Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said. "So we are very aware of that." No NFL team has more rookie starts than the Dolphins, with 66. The Browns have 43. The Giants have 29. "I understand our team and I understand that we have seven games left and the college season has one more and it's not even really that," Hafley said. "It's just these guys have not stopped since their playoff game or bowl game and then Combine and then pro days and then rookie mini camp, OTAs and then they finally caught a breath, so they haven't stopped for two years. So it's very real, right? So it's recovery, it's sleep, it's us doing a really good job of not just the physical part, but the mental fatigue is very, very real." Key Dolphins rookies include: OL Kadyn Proctor , CB Chris Johnson , LB Jacob Rodriguez , WR Caleb Douglas , TE Will Kacmarek and S Michael Taaffe . The Dolphins drafted 13 rookies. And they've added six more since the season began. One draft pick has been cut. One is on injured reserve. Three are on practice squad. Miami Dolphins currently have 14 rostered rookies On the one hand, young Dolphins are improving and learning the pro game and schemes. On the other hand, a team with an average age of 25.6 — 25.6! — has a lot to learn. "With a young team, it's been a little bit slower, but they're really starting to pick it up," Hafley said. As for this infamous "rookie wall?" "I've got to take care of my body and know I still have a whole half of the season to play," said Johnson, the cornerback. "And like you said, I've heard about it from multiple teammates. But I feel like it is what it is. I love playing football, so I'm going to just hopefully keep my body healthy for as long as possible and continue playing." Hard-hitting rookie fullback DJ Herman said: "Hot tubs and cold tubs and the sauna, make sure my body's warm, more stretching. So after multiple weeks of just kind of getting into a groove and making sure that what works and what doesn't, you kind of just get a basis of like, all right, this works and this doesn't." top.title: Tyson Fury ‘cleared’ to fight Anthony Joshua after clarification on schizophrenia diagnosis
top.description: Tyson Fury has reportedly been medically cleared to box Anthony Joshua , after confusion around a possible schizophrenia diagnosis. Fury is scheduled to face his fellow British heavyweight on 11 December , as the pair headline at Cardiff’s Principallity stadium in a fight years in the making. However, the bout appeared to be under threat this week, as quotes from Tyson Fury – a new Netflix documentary – did the rounds. The quotes saw Fury’s wife Paris suggesting that the boxer was once diagnosed with schizophrenia. Tyson Fury in 2026 (PA) That prompted Robert Smith, general secretary of the British Boxing Board of Control (BBBofC), to tell the BBC: “We are in the process of dealing with the matter, but if there are any medical issues we wouldn’t let anyone box. It doesn’t matter if it’s Tyson Fury or not, it could be anybody. I’m fairly confident he will be absolutely fine. We’re dealing with it now and we’ll have an answer very shortly.” Paris soon released a statement that read : “I want to clarify a statement I made in the original version of the Tyson Fury documentary. I recalled a conversation from many years ago when discussing Tyson’s condition and I used the word ‘schizophrenic’. Whilst Tyson did show some symptoms associated with schizophrenia, he doesn’t have this condition and has never received a diagnosis. “Mental health is complex, and it isn't always easy to find the right words, especially when you're living it with someone you love. I’m so proud of Tyson for really opening up in this documentary and want to say thank you for all the support we’ve received as a family.” Meanwhile, Netflix said: “Following new information shared by the family relating to Tyson’s official mental health diagnosis, we have worked alongside them to update the documentary accordingly ahead of launch.” The film was released on Friday, and the scene in question had been reported on earlier this week, following preview screenings earlier in November . Fury will finally face Anthony Joshua on 11 December (PA Wire) Friday also brought a report from journalist Gareth A Davies, who tweeted: “Tyson Fury’s medicals were all cleared by the Boxing Board on Thursday evening. His promoter was informed Friday morning. top.title: Leipzig only open to January sale of Antonio Nusa for an irresistible offer
top.description: Leipzig only open to January sale of Antonio Nusa for an irresistible offer RB Leipzig will only consider sell Antonio Nusa in January if an irresistible offer arrives for the winger. Nusa is attracting interest from Europe's biggest clubs after a brilliant start to the season in Leipzig. The 21-year-old has five goals and seven assists in 10 Bundesliga appearances, and has scored three times in the Champions League. That return includes a double against Lens in midweek. His influence for Norway is also increasing. Nusa was on target against Wales during November's international break and has now scored 10 goals in 36 caps. He's become an important figure for Ståle Solbakken's side, alongside Erling Haaland and Martin Odegaard. Arsenal have made Nusa a top target as the Gunners look to sign a left-winger, while Paris Saint-Germain have also shortlisted the Norwegian. PSG want to sign a winger in January, following season-ending ACL injuries to Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue. Bayern Munich are also monitoring his performances this season. Leipzig are set to hold firm until the summer, report Sky Germany , unless the German side receives an offer above €100m (£83.5m). Leipzig need to recoup around €100m in the upcoming transfer windows and would only consider a mid-season sale, should that offer arrive. The Bundesliga side want Nusa to remain and help their bid for Champions League qualification, before his future is reassessed in the summer. Leipzig expect him to stay until at least the end of the season.

top.title: How tight ends give Delaware football more ways to attack defenses
top.description: At certain times and places, the tight end has been an endangered species on college football fields. It’s not uncommon to see an offense line up without a tight end, a position that requires sturdy blocking ability plus the elusiveness and dexterity to catch passes. The Air Raid and Run-and-Shoot offenses are among those that typically don’t employ someone at that position. Spread offenses can go with or without them, but Delaware coach Ryan Carty has found value in having tight ends in is schemes. It was never more obvious than in Delaware’s Nov. 21 Conference USA game at New Mexico State. Tight ends caught all five of Nick Minicucci’s touchdown passes in the 42-30 victory, which was Delaware’s sixth of the season and made the Blue Hens bowl eligible. “It was a great day for the tight ends,” sophomore tight end Scott Moore said. “Five touchdowns for a room, it’s great. We love that the tight ends got so much love that game . . . We just happen to be open. We’re not always the first option.” Moore snared three of those TD passes, from 19 yards in the second quarter, 9 yards in the third quarter and a nifty 20-yarder when it appeared Minicucci was running before flipping the ball over approaching defenders to the wide-open Moore. Dover High grad Elijah Sessoms caught a 4-yarder for Delaware’s first TD and Josh Humes, the transfer from Coastal Carolina, grabbed a 44-yarder in the fourth quarter. The Blue Hens (6-5 overall, 4-3 CUSA) will likely need similar contributions when Jacksonville State (8-3, 6-1) visits Delaware Stadium in the regular-season Nov. 28. Kickoff is at 3:30 p.m. with the CBS Sports Network televising. “I think the biggest thing for us offensively, the way we see it,” Carty said, “is we want to have the ability to, as much as we can, stay in 11 personnel -- one tight end, three receivers, one running back -- so that we can move down the field without changing personnel as much. We can do whatever we need out of that.” When Carty was offensive coordinator at Sam Houston from 2018-21, there were times he used tight ends less in his spread offense. That was more, he said, because of the personnel he had, adding many of the Texas high schools from which Sam Houston recruited ran Air Raid offenses and, therefore, didn’t produce as many tight end prospects. “When you take a tight end off the field,” Carty said, “you kind of limit a lot of the things that you can do in the run game. You can't add that extra hat [for blocking] as well. You also limit what you can do in the protection game.” Delaware will also sometimes line up in 12 personnel groupings – one running back and two tight ends. Moore, who played high school football in Kansas in a Delaware Wing-T offense, appreciates the value Delaware puts on the position. top.description: “A lot of positives” – Thomas Frank reacts to his first win in charge of Crystal Palace Crystal Palace 2-1 Real Sociedad, Thomas Frank Targets Turning Point After First Win Thomas Frank has been in the job for two matches and already has something Crystal Palace badly needed, a win. The 2-1 victory over Real Sociedad does not change Palace being bottom of the Premier League, but it does give the new manager a result he can point to and, more importantly, a response from his players. Palace were behind in the second half after Chelsea loanee Mamadou Sarr scored for Sociedad. From there, the game shifted. Jon Martin picked up a second yellow card, Sociedad went down to 10 men, and Palace finally took control of the situation. top.title: Arsenic In The Water: Thailand Presses Myanmar Over Mining Pollution
top.description: As pollution mounts in its rivers, food and water, Thailand is pressing neighbouring Myanmar to tackle unregulated mining, while urging China to exert its influence in the war-ravaged nation. Tap water supplies to 14 villages in Mae Sai district near the Myanmar border were suspended earlier this month after arsenic levels were found to be nearly 30 times government limits. Bangkok this week hosted the first Thai-Myanmar working group on the issue — also attended by the Chinese ambassador — where it said tests proved rare-earth and gold mines in Myanmar were causing the pollution downstream. The two sides agreed to joint water sampling on the Kok and Sai rivers. This photo taken on June 5, 2026 shows Wan Wiriya, assistant professor from Chiang Mai University, showing the results of an arsenic level test from a water sample (C) taken from the Kok River, next to a control sample of drinking water (R) near the the northern Thai city of Chiang Rai. Photo by LILLIAN SUWANRUMPHA / AFP But there was no public agreement to Thailand’s request for a six-month suspension of operations, and how one could be implemented remains unclear, with Myanmar’s military not in full control. Bangkok is also looking to China, the main importer of rare-earth materials from Myanmar, to pressure private Chinese operators, as a months-long concern becomes increasingly urgent. Authorities warned residents this week against eating certain shellfish and other river species after tests in northern and northeastern Thailand found dangerous levels of arsenic and lead. Saengwaree Suvirakan, a farmer from Tha Ton in Chiang Mai province who joined a protest in Bangkok this week, said fish stocks were declining in any case. “Now with the mines the fish are all gone,” she said. ‘Not from nature’ This photo taken on June 4, 2026 shows fishermen and their boats near the confluence of the Kok River and Mekong River in Chiang Saen, northern Thailand’s Chiang Rai province. Photo by LILLIAN SUWANRUMPHA / AFP At the joint talks, Thai ministers said high arsenic levels in the Kok and Sai rivers could only have come from rare-earth and gold mines on the Myanmar side. “Arsenic does not come from nature, it came from mining sites. The source was from (Myanmar’s) Shan state, no-one disagrees,” Science Minister Yodchanan Wongsawat said. But how to tackle it remains an issue. Thanapon Piman, senior research fellow at the Stockholm Environment Institute (SEI), welcomed the agreement on joint sampling sites. “This is going to be a first step to agree on the evidence, otherwise you cannot move to the next step, like stopping mining activity,” he told AFP. But Myanmar intervening to stop mining would be “really difficult”, he added. Multiple ethnic armed groups have been operating there for decades, while a 2021 military coup sparked an ongoing civil war. It's the place to be in the city to be, with luxury fashion flagships lining the blocks and supercars speeding through the streets that surround them. But some of its spots are more keen on keeping it low key. One example is COTE, a Korean steakhouse that plays its music at a rarely reasonable level to allow for conversations. That made it the perfect place for Miami's Nikola Jović to host OKC's Nikola Topić the night before their two teams faced off. It’s tradition for a Serbian NBA player to do so whenever another is in town. They talked in their native language over a Michelin-star meal, and basketball wasn’t the sole subject. I love him to death." Jović was alluding to what has been a difficult start to Topić’s NBA career. One where the third-year guard has played in just 22 total games while overcoming a torn ACL , testicular cancer , a back procedure and a few other setbacks along the way. But it’s important to turn to family when faced with adversity, and Topić is part of a special one. He’s part of a family of six active Serbian NBA players. And while that number isn't strong, the bond is. "It definitely means a lot," Topić told The Oklahoman on Wednesday. "There are not a lot of us, so we have to stick together. They're super helpful. nigeria.title: Full list: Italy unveils 14 African countries eligible for work visas
nigeria.description: Italy has listed 14 African countries whose citizens are eligible to apply for work visas under its 2026–2028 immigration programme, offering employment opportunities to foreign workers across several sectors of its economy. Nigeria is among the African countries on the list, alongside Ghana, Senegal, Morocco, Egypt and 10 others. The programme forms part of Italy’s broader labour migration policy, which seeks to admit foreign workers to address labour shortages and meet the country’s employment needs. Under the programme, the Italian government has reserved 25,000 work permits annually for citizens of 38 designated countries, including the 14 African nations. The African countries named are: Algeria Ivory Coast Egypt Ethiopia The Gambia Ghana Mali Morocco Mauritius Niger Nigeria Senegal Sudan Tunisia. The employment opportunities cover sectors including agriculture, forestry, fishing, food production, manufacturing, construction, wholesale and retail trade, hospitality, tourism, transportation, logistics, healthcare and social assistance. According to the Italian Ministry of Labour and Social Policies, the immigration programme provides for a total of 497,550 foreign workers to enter Italy between 2026 and 2028. The allocation is divided into 164,850 workers for 2026, 165,850 for 2027 and 166,850 for 2028. The figures cover seasonal and non-seasonal employment as well as self-employment. However, inclusion on the list does not automatically guarantee a work visa. Applicants must secure employment from an Italian employer, who is generally required to apply for the relevant work authorisation, known as nulla osta , before the worker proceeds with the visa application. For the 2026 allocation, applications for seasonal agricultural jobs were scheduled to open on January 12, while those for seasonal tourism jobs were scheduled for February 9. Applications for non-seasonal employment under the relevant categories were scheduled for February 16 and 18, 2026. The programme is part of Italy’s efforts to address labour shortages through regulated migration while strengthening cooperation with countries of origin. nigeria.title: UK Reform leader vows to scrap Graduate visa route used by 20,478 Nigerians
nigeria.description: UK Reform UK leader, Nigel Farage, has vowed to scrap the United Kingdom’s Graduate visa route if his party wins power, a move that could affect thousands of Nigerians who use the scheme to remain in the country after completing their studies. Farage announced the proposal in a post on X on Thursday, arguing that the route allows foreign graduates to stay in the UK for two years after completing their degrees, competing with British workers for entry level jobs or potentially claiming asylum. Figures published by the UK Home Office on November 26 showed that 20,478 Nigerian nationals received grants under the Graduate route in the year to September 2026, making Nigerians the third largest group of beneficiaries. Indian nationals topped the list with 66,552 grants, followed by Pakistanis with 24,768. The three nationalities accounted for about 69 per cent of all grants recorded during the period. The Graduate route allows international students who have completed eligible courses at UK universities to remain in the country and work or look for employment without needing an immediate job offer or sponsorship. Reform UK’s home affairs spokesman, Zia Yusuf, has described the scheme as “a scam on the British people” and proposed replacing it with a 30 day period for graduates to secure a qualifying job that meets an economic value test. The party said about 800,000 Graduate visas, including those issued to dependants, had been granted since the route was introduced in July 2021. Yusuf also cited Home Office figures showing that 5,130 asylum claims were made by people who had previously held Graduate visas in the year to June 2026, twice the number recorded in the preceding year. The pledge comes as the Labour government is already preparing to reduce the standard duration of the Graduate visa from two years to 18 months from January 1, 2027. The change will not apply to graduates from institutions that meet certain compliance and labour market outcome standards. However, Reform UK has yet to clarify how its proposed abolition would affect people who already hold Graduate visas or international students currently studying in the country. The latest Home Office figures also showed a decline in the number of Nigerian students receiving sponsored study visas. Grants to Nigerian nationals fell by 34 per cent to 19,734 in the year to September 2026, representing about six per cent of the total. nigeria.title: Saudi Strike Kills 11 In Yemen
nigeria.description: A Saudi strike killed 11 people on Friday in western Yemen, Houthi media said, a day after an attack by the Iran-backed movement on an oil refinery in Saudi Arabia. A Saudi-led coalition backing Yemen’s internationally recognised government has been regularly bombing areas controlled by the armed group since the country’s civil war reignited over the summer. In response, Houthi forces have been targeting the oil-rich kingdom almost daily, hitting energy facilities, airports and the financial district of the capital, Riyadh. Saudi warplanes carried out a raid on a residential building in the city of Al-Turba in Taiz governorate on Friday, killing “11 citizens, most of them children,” the Houthis’ Saba news agency said, citing a local source. The agency also reported strikes targeting fuel tanks in the Saada region, the movement’s birthplace and stronghold. Smoke billows from the Yemeni capital Sanaa on November 26, 2026 after Houthi media reported a series of Saudi airstrikes against territories held by the Iran-backed group, hours after it struck Riyadh. Photo by AFP On Thursday, the Houthis targeted the Jazan refinery in southern Saudi Arabia, killing a Nepalese worker and injuring several other people, according to the Saudi Press Agency (SPA). The attack also triggered a fire that led to the shutdown of the facility, the SPA said. Yemen plunged back into war in July, after years of relative calm, opening a new front in the Middle East war. Hostilities intensified in September when the Houthis, who already controlled the most densely populated parts of Yemen, seized the western coastline overlooking the strategic Bab el-Mandeb strait on the Red Sea. The Houthis are now advancing toward Aden, a major southern city where the government has taken refuge after being driven out of the capital Sanaa in 2015. Since the conflict resumed, fighting in Yemen has killed more than 2,300 people and displaced over 364,000, according to the United Nations. nigeria.title: UN warns of worsening hunger in northern Nigeria, 15 other areas
nigeria.description: By Enitan Abdultawab The United Nations has warned of worsening hunger across 16 regions of the world over the next six months, identifying northern Nigeria, Sudan, South Sudan, Somalia and Yemen as areas facing the highest risk of acute food insecurity. The warning was contained in a joint report by the Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) and the World Food Programme (WFP), which attributed the growing food crisis to armed conflicts, climate extremes, economic shocks and declining humanitarian assistance. The report, released on Friday, covers the period from December 2026 to May 2027 and cautioned that conditions could deteriorate further in several African countries as conflict and extreme weather events continue to disrupt livelihoods and food production. It identified Sudan and South Sudan as countries where famine remains a plausible risk, particularly in parts of North Darfur. The agencies also expressed concern over rising political violence, noting that incidents had increased by more than 15 per cent compared with the same period last year. The development, according to the report, has triggered significant displacement in recent months, particularly in South Sudan and Yemen, further worsening the humanitarian situation. It also highlighted a sharp decline in humanitarian funding to the five countries facing the highest levels of concern. entertainment.title: Israel Olaleye: How Can Young Nigerians Buy Land & Properties Legitimately Today?
entertainment.description: Young man with a hard hat holding a red for sale sign outside a building by Pavel Danilyuk for Pexels . My parents’ generation mostly bought land the way their parents did. Someone in the family knew someone in the village. An uncle walked the boundaries. The community remembered who owned what, and if anything went wrong, you had a face to go back to. However, my generation buys land on Instagram. I do not say that to mock anyone. I sell land for a living. When I started in real estate sales in 2023, two years after finishing a Mathematics degree at the University of Ibadan, I assumed buyers would care most about price and location. They do care. But what I hear most often is fear, dressed up as questions. Can I trust you? Is this land real? What happens if I miss a payment? After I pay, will someone come and ask me for more money? A prospective buyer once asked me, before anything else, whether community or family payments would follow after she paid for her plot. She was not asking about the land. She was asking whether the price I quoted was the real price. She had good reason to ask. Lagos State’s Property Protection Law of 2016 made it an offence to demand levies for construction on someone else’s property. Yet the same law still allows a land-owning family, with the family head’s authority, to collect a customary fee for possession, the payment many people know as a “foundation levy”. So the honest answer to her question is not a simple yes or no. It depends on the land, the family, and what has been written down. Most first-time buyers have never been told any of this. That is the gap I keep coming back to. Nobody taught us how to buy land. We learned how to save. Some of us learned how to invest in stocks, crypto or a side business. But land, the asset our parents spoke about with the most respect, has no manual. The people who used to stand in for the manual–the uncle, the community, the family lawyer everyone trusted–are often not part of how we buy anymore. So we improvise. A prospect once told me she had gone through my Instagram page carefully before she agreed to speak with me. She was checking whether I was consistent, whether my posts matched what I said on the phone, whether I had been around long enough to be real. I was flattered. Then I was worried. Because if a social media page has become part of a buyer’s due diligence, then a polished page has also become one of the easiest ways to deceive her. Instagram cannot tell you who owns a piece of land. Only a search at the land registry, done by your own lawyer, can begin to tell you that. Instagram cannot tell you whether a plot sits under government acquisition or on a planned road. A surveyor who charts the coordinates and checks them against official maps can. entertainment.title: M.Inc PR Joins Industry Stakeholders to Explore Africa’s Credit Economy at ACE 2026
entertainment.description: A cross section of industry leaders and stakeholders during the fourth edition of Africa Credit Expo 2026 held on Friday, 13 November 2026, at the J. F. Ade Ajayi Main Auditorium, University of Lagos. What will it take to make credit more accessible to African businesses and individuals? At the fourth edition of Africa Credit Expo (ACE) 202 6, stakeholders across financial services, technology, policy, investment and entrepreneurship examined the role of reliable credit information, financial inclusion and collaboration in expanding access to capital. Powered by CreditRegistry and supported by Afreximbank , the Expo was held on Friday, 13 November 2026, at the J. F. Ade Ajayi Main Auditorium, University of Lagos. Themed “Reimagining Africa’s Credit Economy: Unlocking Capital, Trust and Opportunity,” the event provided a platform for conversations on the systems, innovations and partnerships shaping the future of credit across the continent. Building Trust and Expanding Access to Capital Discussions at the Expo explored the role of credible credit information in building trust between lenders and borrowers. Reliable data enables financial institutions to assess risk more effectively and make informed lending decisions, while individuals and businesses with established credit histories are better positioned to demonstrate their credit worthiness. The conversations also considered the financing constraints facing micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs). Despite their contribution to employment and economic activity, many small businesses continue to encounter barriers to affordable financing. Improving access to relevant financial products and strengthening credit information systems remain important to addressing these gaps. Technology, Financial Inclusion and the Next Generation Digital innovation and data intelligence featured prominently in discussions about the future of credit. Alternative credit assessment approaches have the potential to broaden access for individuals and businesses with limited formal credit histories. However, the expansion of digital financial services must be accompanied by responsible lending practices, consumer protection and transparency. The Expo also placed attention on young people through student-focused sessions and discussions on financial literacy. These conversations connected access to credit with the need for individuals to understand financial management, borrowing and long-term wealth creation. This focus reflects the February 2026 memorandum of understanding between CreditRegistry and the University of Lagos, through its Entrepreneurship and Skills Development Centre (ESDC), to integrate the Africa Consumer Credit Academy (ACCA) curriculum into the Centre’s programmes. The initiative is intended to strengthen financial literacy through learning opportunities, mentorship, certification and engagement with industry. entertainment.title: As Nigeria Rethinks Teacher Education, Tunji Olowolafe Makes a Case for Better-Prepared Educators
entertainment.description: What makes a good teacher? Beyond knowing a subject, a good teacher can understand students, inspire confidence, and help young people discover what they are capable of becoming. It was this broader responsibility of educators that Dr. Tunji Olowolafe explored while delivering the 2026 Convocation Lecture at the Sikiru Adetona College of Education, Science and Technology (SACOETEC), Omu-Ajose, Ogun State. Speaking on Monday, 23 November 2026, on the theme “The Dual-Mandate NCE-Degree Programme: Prospects, Challenges and the Future of Teacher Education in Nigeria,” he described the programme as an important opportunity to reposition teacher education. For decades, Colleges of Education depended on university affiliations to award Bachelor’s degrees, despite many possessing the academic capacity to run such programmes. The Federal Colleges of Education Act 2023 changed this, empowering eligible institutions to award degrees independently. Under the Dual-Mandate programme, students can complete three years of NCE training and proceed to another two years for a Bachelor’s degree in Education. Dr. Olowolafe explained that combining practical teaching skills with deeper academic knowledge would produce better-prepared educators. However, he cautioned that institutional autonomy must be supported by sustained funding, improved curricula and professional development. With Nigeria facing an estimated shortage of one million teachers, he also called for greater integration of vocational education, artificial intelligence and digital skills into learning. “AI can explain a quadratic equation at midnight, but it cannot offer the steady, empathetic guidance of a caring adult,” he said, emphasizing that artificial intelligence must complement, not replace, the human qualities of effective teaching. During the lecture, Dr. Olowolafe announced that the Tunji Olowolafe Foundation would establish a fully equipped, solar-powered Gbemisola Olowolafe Memorial ICT Centre (GOMTECH) with high-speed internet connectivity at SACOETEC. The Foundation is also committed to recognising academic excellence and outstanding teaching at the College. This includes recognising the College’s first-class degree graduates and NCE distinction holders, alongside the overall best NCE and degree graduates. Lecturers, selected based on student ratings, will also be honoured for their teaching contributions. The initiative builds on the Foundation’s existing investment in education, including Project Digi-Teach at Ekiti State University and GOMTECH in Are-Ekiti. For Dr. Olowolafe, the commitment to educators is also deeply personal. His mother was a teacher, his elder sister taught for years at Baptist Academy, Lagos, and his late wife, Gbemisola Olowolafe, was a lifelong educator. He recalled the influence of teachers who shaped his own experience, particularly Mr. Soewu of Methodist Boys’ High School , whose patience helped students understand difficult concepts without humiliation. Then you probably remember that voice. Deep, commanding and unmistakable, it often came with his signature red cap, traditional Igbo attire and a generous helping of proverbs. The actor was just as memorable away from the screen, where his sharp wit, outspoken nature and candid opinions made him a fascinating personality in interviews. He was never one to shy away from saying exactly what he thought, and that straightforwardness became another part of what audiences remembered about him. For generations of Nollywood viewers, Pete Edochie was the actor they could recognise before he had even finished his first sentence. He became one of Nigerian cinema’s most familiar faces, often playing kings, chiefs, fathers and respected elders. His breakthrough came in 1987 when he portrayed Okonkwo in the television adaptation of Chinua Achebe ‘s Things Fall Apart , a performance that helped establish him as one of Nollywood’s most respected actors. The veteran actor passed away in Enugu yesterday, on Wednesday, 25 November 2026, at the age of 79, following a prolonged battle with prostate cancer. Born in Zaria and originally from Ifite Nteje in Anambra State, Edochie began his career in broadcasting in 1967, eventually rising to become Deputy Managing Director of the Anambra Broadcasting Service. He went on to feature in hundreds of films, including Igodo , The Egg of Life and Lionheart . His performance was so transformative that, for generations of viewers, Edochie and Okonkwo became inseparable. In fashion, the conversation often begins with style, but it rarely ends there. Quality, affordability, accessibility and the story behind what we wear are increasingly becoming part of how consumers make their choices. For Alero Ebigbeyi, these are not just considerations; they are the principles shaping her latest venture, HÉYCH. The Nigerian fashion and clothing brand officially opened its retail store on November 10, bringing together fashion enthusiasts, media executives, influencers, friends and industry personalities for an introduction to the brand and its collections. With over 30 years of experience in this industry, I understand the importance of quality, production standards and delivering value to customers,” she says. entertainment.description: Nollywood icon Pete Edochie, MON, who passed away at the age of 79 in Enugu. Photo Credit: Pete Edochie/Instagram Nollywood and the wider African entertainment community are mourning the loss of one of their most respected screen icons, Pete Edochie , MON, who passed away on Wednesday, 25 November 2026,at the age of 79. According to an official statement released on behalf of the family by his eldest son, Leo Pete Edochie , the veteran actor and retired broadcaster departed this life at 12:30 a.m. in Enugu, Nigeria, following a protracted battle with prostate cancer. Born on 7 March 1947 in Zaria, Kaduna State, and hailing from Akamnato, Ifite Nteje in Anambra State, Pete Edochie began his career in broadcasting long before becoming a household name on television and cinema screens. At age 20, in 1967, he joined the Eastern Nigeria Broadcasting Service (ENBS)—later the Anambra Broadcasting Service (ABS)—rising steadily through the ranks to serve as Director of Programmes and Deputy Managing Director. His defining breakthrough came in 1987 when he portrayed the fierce, tragic hero Okonkwo in the Nigerian Television Authority’s (NTA) acclaimed television adaptation of Chinua Achebe ‘s Things Fall Apart. His commanding presence and deep, resonant voice earned him international recognition—including a dedicated delegation interview from the BBC—and cemented his place in Nigerian television history. Over a screen career spanning nearly four decades, Pete Edochie became synonymous with authority,traditional wisdom, and unforgettable Igbo proverbs. Whether playing stern monarchs, principled elders, or complex patriarchs, he delivered every line with unmistakable gravitas. His extensive filmography includes standout appearances in classics and modern hits alike, such as Things Fall Apart (1987), Igodo (1999), Egg of Life (2003), Oracle (2003), Billionaires Club (2003), End of Money (2005), Lionheart (2018)—where he starred as Chief Ernest Obiagu alongside Genevieve Nnaji—Unroyal (2020), and Foreigner’s God (2022). In recognition of his immense contributions to Nigerian arts and culture, he was conferred with the national honour of Member of the Order of the Niger (MON) in 2003 by former President Olusegun Obasanjo,alongside the Africa Magic Viewers’ Choice Awards (AMVCA) Industry Merit Award and lifetime achievement honours from the Africa Film Academy and the African Film Festival (TAFF). sports.title: Patriots defense preparing for every quarterback possibility with Chargers
sports.description: The New England Patriots are not the only team facing quarterback questions heading into Week 12. The Los Angeles Chargers, their opponent on Sunday, are in the same boat. Starting QB Justin Herbert remains in concussion protocol and was a no-show at practice both Wednesday and Thursday. With his status in question, backup D.J. Uiagalelei might be elevated into the starting role. Given that uncertainty, the Patriots defense is faced with a question: who to prepare for? “That’s a question that gets asked a lot: ‘You don’t know if a quarterback’s going to play or not, do you prepare for all of them?’ It’s lot about us,” defensive coordinator Zak Kuhr explained earlier this week. “Obviously, we know a lot more about Herbert’s play style than the next two guys, D.J. and Jake [Browning], if they make Jake active. But they are aware of their play styles. Obviously, there’s a lot more tape of Herbert, but everybody’s aware of the contingency plans. We went over that again [Wednesday], the contingency plans if we get news if something else changes.” Kuhr likened the situation to preparing for Denver Broncos backup quarterback Jarrett Stidham ahead of last year’s AFC Championship Game. That contest came two weeks after New England’s most recent meeting with Herbert, whose offense was held to three points in the wild card round. Uiagalelei was inactive as a member of the Chargers’ practice squad that day. Now, 10 months later, he is in line to potentially get his first career start and add to a résumé consisting of a mere 21 regular season snaps — all of them in a loss to the Texans earlier this season — as well as two pass completions on seven attempts for 24 yards and a touchdown. Despite the limited output so far, the Patriots have to familiarize themselves with the 25-year-old former undrafted free agent. And in the process of doing so, they have seen some differences to Los Angeles’ regular starter. “Strong arm. I would say more from the pocket than Herbert,” Kuhr said about his game. “Obviously, some inexperience. But he made some plays in college; obviously, he’s made a roster. So, I would say he’s a professional, he’s going to take advantage of his opportunity just like every backup quarterback does.”

sports.title: Dolphins counting on rookies to push through NFL's 'rookie wall'
sports.description: MIAMI GARDENS — It's Week 12 in the NFL and Kadyn Proctor of the Miami Dolphins is one of the many rookies who played 12 regular-season college games last year. Now, Proctor had three more games because Alabama always plays extra games. But the point here is that all NFL rookies hit the proverbial "rookie wall" at some point in late November or December. "I feel wonderful," Proctor said this week. "I've been telling my teammates. They've informed me about the rookie wall. I said I'm not going to hit it." The Dolphins (1-9) host the Jets (3-8) on Sunday, Nov. 29 at Hard Rock Stadium. And no team in the NFL has relied more on rookies than the Dolphins this season. "The wall's a concern for a big part of our team that are rookies and that are playing a lot of snaps, right?" Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said. "So we are very aware of that." No NFL team has more rookie starts than the Dolphins, with 66. The Browns have 43. The Giants have 29. "I understand our team and I understand that we have seven games left and the college season has one more and it's not even really that," Hafley said. "It's just these guys have not stopped since their playoff game or bowl game and then Combine and then pro days and then rookie mini camp, OTAs and then they finally caught a breath, so they haven't stopped for two years. So it's very real, right? So it's recovery, it's sleep, it's us doing a really good job of not just the physical part, but the mental fatigue is very, very real." Key Dolphins rookies include: OL Kadyn Proctor , CB Chris Johnson , LB Jacob Rodriguez , WR Caleb Douglas , TE Will Kacmarek and S Michael Taaffe . The Dolphins drafted 13 rookies. And they've added six more since the season began. One draft pick has been cut. One is on injured reserve. Three are on practice squad. Miami Dolphins currently have 14 rostered rookies On the one hand, young Dolphins are improving and learning the pro game and schemes. On the other hand, a team with an average age of 25.6 — 25.6! — has a lot to learn. "With a young team, it's been a little bit slower, but they're really starting to pick it up," Hafley said. As for this infamous "rookie wall?" "I've got to take care of my body and know I still have a whole half of the season to play," said Johnson, the cornerback. "And like you said, I've heard about it from multiple teammates. But I feel like it is what it is. I love playing football, so I'm going to just hopefully keep my body healthy for as long as possible and continue playing." Hard-hitting rookie fullback DJ Herman said: "Hot tubs and cold tubs and the sauna, make sure my body's warm, more stretching. So after multiple weeks of just kind of getting into a groove and making sure that what works and what doesn't, you kind of just get a basis of like, all right, this works and this doesn't." sports.title: Tyson Fury ‘cleared’ to fight Anthony Joshua after clarification on schizophrenia diagnosis
sports.description: Tyson Fury has reportedly been medically cleared to box Anthony Joshua , after confusion around a possible schizophrenia diagnosis. Fury is scheduled to face his fellow British heavyweight on 11 December , as the pair headline at Cardiff’s Principallity stadium in a fight years in the making. However, the bout appeared to be under threat this week, as quotes from Tyson Fury – a new Netflix documentary – did the rounds. The quotes saw Fury’s wife Paris suggesting that the boxer was once diagnosed with schizophrenia. Tyson Fury in 2026 (PA) That prompted Robert Smith, general secretary of the British Boxing Board of Control (BBBofC), to tell the BBC: “We are in the process of dealing with the matter, but if there are any medical issues we wouldn’t let anyone box. It doesn’t matter if it’s Tyson Fury or not, it could be anybody. I’m fairly confident he will be absolutely fine. We’re dealing with it now and we’ll have an answer very shortly.” Paris soon released a statement that read : “I want to clarify a statement I made in the original version of the Tyson Fury documentary. I recalled a conversation from many years ago when discussing Tyson’s condition and I used the word ‘schizophrenic’. Whilst Tyson did show some symptoms associated with schizophrenia, he doesn’t have this condition and has never received a diagnosis. “Mental health is complex, and it isn't always easy to find the right words, especially when you're living it with someone you love. I’m so proud of Tyson for really opening up in this documentary and want to say thank you for all the support we’ve received as a family.” Meanwhile, Netflix said: “Following new information shared by the family relating to Tyson’s official mental health diagnosis, we have worked alongside them to update the documentary accordingly ahead of launch.” The film was released on Friday, and the scene in question had been reported on earlier this week, following preview screenings earlier in November . Fury will finally face Anthony Joshua on 11 December (PA Wire) Friday also brought a report from journalist Gareth A Davies, who tweeted: “Tyson Fury’s medicals were all cleared by the Boxing Board on Thursday evening. His promoter was informed Friday morning. sports.title: How tight ends give Delaware football more ways to attack defenses
sports.description: At certain times and places, the tight end has been an endangered species on college football fields. It’s not uncommon to see an offense line up without a tight end, a position that requires sturdy blocking ability plus the elusiveness and dexterity to catch passes. The Air Raid and Run-and-Shoot offenses are among those that typically don’t employ someone at that position. Spread offenses can go with or without them, but Delaware coach Ryan Carty has found value in having tight ends in is schemes. It was never more obvious than in Delaware’s Nov. 21 Conference USA game at New Mexico State. Tight ends caught all five of Nick Minicucci’s touchdown passes in the 42-30 victory, which was Delaware’s sixth of the season and made the Blue Hens bowl eligible. “It was a great day for the tight ends,” sophomore tight end Scott Moore said. “Five touchdowns for a room, it’s great. We love that the tight ends got so much love that game . . . We just happen to be open. We’re not always the first option.” Moore snared three of those TD passes, from 19 yards in the second quarter, 9 yards in the third quarter and a nifty 20-yarder when it appeared Minicucci was running before flipping the ball over approaching defenders to the wide-open Moore. Dover High grad Elijah Sessoms caught a 4-yarder for Delaware’s first TD and Josh Humes, the transfer from Coastal Carolina, grabbed a 44-yarder in the fourth quarter. The Blue Hens (6-5 overall, 4-3 CUSA) will likely need similar contributions when Jacksonville State (8-3, 6-1) visits Delaware Stadium in the regular-season Nov. 28. Kickoff is at 3:30 p.m. with the CBS Sports Network televising. “I think the biggest thing for us offensively, the way we see it,” Carty said, “is we want to have the ability to, as much as we can, stay in 11 personnel -- one tight end, three receivers, one running back -- so that we can move down the field without changing personnel as much. We can do whatever we need out of that.” When Carty was offensive coordinator at Sam Houston from 2018-21, there were times he used tight ends less in his spread offense. That was more, he said, because of the personnel he had, adding many of the Texas high schools from which Sam Houston recruited ran Air Raid offenses and, therefore, didn’t produce as many tight end prospects. “When you take a tight end off the field,” Carty said, “you kind of limit a lot of the things that you can do in the run game. You can't add that extra hat [for blocking] as well. You also limit what you can do in the protection game.” Delaware will also sometimes line up in 12 personnel groupings – one running back and two tight ends. sports.description: Motorsport photo With F1 close to signing off on the overarching tenets of its 2030 return to V8 power units, some of its leading drivers have fleshed out ideas of how to make those into a compelling product. F1 is set to move to all-new turbo V8 engines in 2030, with a smaller electric unit of up to 200kW and sustainable fuel. That should make engines simpler, cheaper and lighter, and therefore reduce the reliance on energy from the battery compared to today's oft-criticised formula. By signing off the V8 move at the next FIA World Motor Sport Council gathering in Shanghai on 12 December, F1 and the FIA are giving themselves time to properly flesh out the chassis and aerodynamic regulations that should work in unison with the V8 power units to produce a better on-track show. Last weekend's Las Vegas Grand Prix has given the series some food for though about what it really wants from its next rules cycle. At the Las Vegas street circuit, F1 delivered an absorbing spectacle featuring a record 35 lead changes, aided by a combination of the powerful slipstreaming effect and the boost mode from the power unit, which led to so-called yo-yo racing as the lead car often ended up a sitting duck on the straight. While there was debate on whether that's the kind of show F1 wants to see more of, or whether Vegas was too artificial for its own good, it further highlighted the importance of developing a combination of power unit parameters and aerodynamics overtaking aids that can be fine-tuned on a race-to-race basis to deliver a solid spectacle without making overtaking too trivial either. It prompted Williams driver and Grand Prix Drivers' Association director Carlos Sainz to come up with an intriguing idea on how to tune a DRS-like overtaking system for 2030, suggesting a straightline boost that aids chasing drivers coming right out of the corners. That would offset the loss of cornering speed from following a car in its dirty air. "I think for 2030 I have an idea of where I would like it to be," Sainz explained. sports.title: Hamilton Is Two Races From Beating Leclerc on Points, Poles and Podiums—a First
sports.description: Lewis Hamilton leads Ferrari teammate Charles Leclerc on points, Grand Prix podiums and poles with two races left in the 2026 Formula 1 season. If he holds on in Qatar and Abu Dhabi, he will be the first teammate to finish a full season ahead of Leclerc on all three, a point Autosport made this week. Our own check of every season Leclerc has raced in F1 backs it up. Where the Ferrari Teammates Stand After Las Vegas After 21 rounds, Hamilton has 267 points to Leclerc’s 250, in the official standings . Those totals include sprint points. On Grand Prix podiums, it’s seven to six. Hamilton’s came in China, Canada, Monaco, Barcelona, Britain, Bahrain and Mexico, and one of them was a win in Barcelona. Leclerc’s came in Australia, Japan, Britain, Belgium, Singapore and Austin, with his win at Silverstone. Sprint podiums aren’t in that count. Add them, and it’s level at 10 each: Hamilton has three sprint podiums and Leclerc four, by our count of the official results. The pole count is the thinnest margin: one to none. Hamilton took his first Ferrari pole in Mexico City, by 0.009 seconds from George Russell, with Leclerc third. It would be a big turnaround from 2025, Hamilton’s first year in red. Leclerc beat him 242 points to 156 that season and took seven Grand Prix podiums, while Hamilton didn’t get one. Las Vegas added to the gap. On the Strip, Leclerc’s late lunge at Turn 7 spun Hamilton out of sixth and earned Leclerc a 10-second penalty. Hamilton fought back to seventh, while Leclerc dropped to 10th. Lewis Hamilton at the Las Vegas GP. Image Credit: Scuderia Ferrari / X Why No Leclerc Teammate Has Done It Before Leclerc has had four full-time teammates since his debut with Sauber in 2018. We counted a teammate as beating him only when they finished a season strictly ahead on all three: championship points, Grand Prix podiums and poles. Marcus Ericsson, his Sauber teammate in 2018, scored nine points to Leclerc’s 39, and neither took a podium or a pole. At Ferrari, Sebastian Vettel trailed him on all three in 2019, then on points and podiums in 2020, a year when neither Ferrari took a pole. Carlos Sainz came closest. In 2021, he beat Leclerc 164.5 points to 159 and four Grand Prix podiums to one, but Leclerc took two poles to Sainz’s none. Leclerc then led Sainz on all three from 2022 to 2024, and Hamilton on all three in 2025. That makes 2026 Hamilton’s to lose. Leclerc can still stop it with a single pole, by finishing on the podium more often than Hamilton in the last two races, or by outscoring him by 17 points or more. Any fight will happen under a warning from the top. Team principal Fred Vasseur was blunt about the Vegas contact after the race, Autosport reported . “It’s unacceptable. It’s a lack of respect for the team, for the sponsors, the same speech as after Mexico.”

sports.title: New Wayne Gretzky Documentary Premieres Today, Revisiting The Stick That Changed Hockey
sports.description: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Wayne Gretzky had already won four Stanley Cups and nine Hart Trophies, including eight consecutively, by the time he made one of the most influential equipment changes in hockey history. In 1990, entering his third season with the Los Angeles Kings, Gretzky ditched the wooden Titan stick he’d used throughout much of his NHL career in favor of a two-piece aluminum stick manufactured by Easton. More than three decades later, the NHL is revisiting that decision in a 24-minute documentary titled The Stick That Changed the Game , scheduled to premiere today at 11 a.m. ET on the league’s YouTube channel. Gretzky wasn’t the first hockey player to use an aluminum stick, but there wasn’t a player on the planet who could do more for the popularity of a piece of hockey equipment. He was coming off a 142-point season with the Kings, and the attention he’d brought to hockey in Southern California made him an ideal candidate to introduce a relatively unconventional product to the masses. According to NHL.com’s Dave Stubbs , Gretzky preferred an unusually stiff shaft and a moderate blade curve. Achieving that level of stiffness with a wooden stick meant carrying some extra weight, something Gretzky generally tried to avoid with his equipment. Easton was able to develop an aluminum model that catered to his preferences. Gretzky’s agent, Mike Barnett, also wanted the stick to be easily recognizable. Easton polished the aluminum shaft to give it the shiny silver appearance that became synonymous with Gretzky’s years in Los Angeles, allowing fans watching on television to immediately recognize that the greatest player in the world was using something different. Gretzky scored twice in the Kings’ season-opening victory over the New York Islanders on Oct. 4, 1990, and went on to register 163 points in 78 games that season, winning his ninth career Art Ross Trophy. The documentary also features current NHL players getting their hands on Gretzky’s old stick. It weighs 614 grams, compared to the 359-gram modern composite stick used for comparison in the film. That’s a pretty substantial difference for players who grew up using composite sticks, especially considering Gretzky’s Easton was designed with weight reduction in mind. Gretzky himself eventually went back to using a wooden stick toward the end of his career with the New York Rangers after investing in the Hespeler hockey equipment company. There are generations of hockey players who have never had to buy a replacement blade, heat the end of a shaft or spend an afternoon trying to get a stubborn wooden plug out of a broken stick. For anyone who grew up doing those things, Friday’s documentary should be a fun watch. For anyone who didn’t, it might be equally entertaining and informative. sports.title: Dan Evans to compete in controversial Gazprom-backed exhibition tournament
sports.description: Retired British tennis player Dan Evans is in the line-up for a highly controversial exhibition tournament which is sponsored by Russian energy giant Gazprom . Gazprom is majority state-owned and has been sanctioned by the UK government for its role in funding Russia’s war in Ukraine, with a 2025 statement saying its profits were “lining Putin’s war chest and facilitating the war”. The company sponsors the annual Northern Palmyra Trophies exhibition, which is held this year from 27-29 November in St Petersburg and features 12 current or former tennis players. Russia has not held any official ATP or WTA Tour events since the invasion of Ukraine in 2022 and Russian and Belarusian players cannot represent their country, instead competing as neutral athletes. However, exhibitions are not covered by the rules governing Tour events and players are free to play in such tournaments on Russian soil. Evans, who retired at Wimbledon this year, has not commented on his decision to take part in the event. The Northern Palmyra Trophies sees two teams face off in a mix of singles and doubles matches, with Evans drawn against world No 11, Russia’s Diana Shnaider, in a Battle of the Sexes-style clash. Frenchmen Adrian Mannarino and Corentin Moutet are also in the line-up, which primarily consists of Russian or Russian-born players. Top-100 players Anastasia Potapova , Kamilla Rakhimova, and Yulia Putintseva , who were all born in Russia, are competing, as is the retired former world No 13 Elena Vesnina . Potapova and Rakhimova have both switched nationality since the war began, with the former now representing Austria and the latter Uzbekistan. Putintseva has represented Kazakhstan since 2012. Russian 17-year-old Anna Pushkareva, compatriot Karen Khachanov , retired Serbian player Jakno Tipsarevic and Kazakhstan’s Alexander Bublik complete the line-up. Former US Open champion Daniil Medvedev competed last year but is absent for 2026. The Netherlands’ Tallon Griekspoor, who is in a relationship with Potapova, sparked a diplomatic incident when he decided to play in last year’s tournament. Dutch Foreign Minister David van Weel issued a public statement urging him to withdraw, to no avail: “It is not forbidden to participate in tournaments in Russia, but I appeal to him not to do so where possible and to look at the moral aspects.” The Russian embassy said it was “deeply concerned” by the “pressure” put on Griekspoor.

technology.title: Europe's AI sovereignty push: Lots of cloud, not much silver lining
technology.description: Europe's IT spending is growing more slowly than the global average, according to Gartner, whose analysts warn that the region's push for tech sovereignty faces commercial and technological obstacles. Gartner forecasts European IT spending of $1.57 trillion in 2027, up 9.9 percent from 2026, compared with worldwide growth of 15 percent to $7.35 trillion. For 2026, it estimates spending growth of 20.7 percent in North America and 13.7 percent in China. "The world seems to be racing towards this AI goal of where the large language model provider is going to be, and the race seems to be between North American-based providers and some Asia Pacific providers," John-David Lovelock, Distinguished VP Analyst at Gartner, told The Register . He said Europe had traditionally trailed in IT uptake. "We saw that happen when global sourcing, cloud, and software as a service all came along. It's down to the pushback against the idea of creative destruction," where new technologies replace old ones. Europe's fastest growing categories are datacenter systems, forecast to grow 29.7 percent in 2027, and infrastructure as a service, at 26.7 percent. Even so, Lovelock does not expect Europe to compete with North America and China on AI investment. "For AI provision, Europe is going to be behind, and there won't be a way to catch up," he said. "The AI datacenters, the large language models, the foundational models, the tools and techniques for building out AI are all being centered outside of Europe, but enterprises don't need to do that. So the question becomes: regardless of where the source of the AI is coming from, can the enterprises actually adopt and use it? In one sense, Europe will be behind in the provision of AI, but it need not be behind in the use." The gap nonetheless complicates Europe's push to reduce its dependence on US technology suppliers. The European Union has introduced new rules to encourage tech buyers to favor sovereign tech over the dominant tech vendors, but Lovelock doubts they will move spending much. "Sovereignty is a wonderful flag that we fly on the front of a building. IT is running in the basement. CIOs are not going to buy a second-best solution that costs more simply because it's sovereign. "They are not going to break any laws, but they are not going to make a decision that puts their company in a worse position at a higher cost. While sovereignty gets [vendors] on the list, it doesn't assure that they get purchased," he told us. Earlier this month, Gartner predicted that by 2029, more than 90 percent of EU organizations will have a digital sovereignty strategy, but argued that a fully sovereign technology stack remains out of reach. "The global technology supply chain is too interconnected, and many critical dependencies cannot be replaced at a commercially viable scale," said Bettina Tratz-Ryan, VP analyst at Gartner. ®

technology.title: AI boom leaves network operators waiting up to 18 months for kit
technology.description: The AI building boom is driving up optical networking equipment prices and stretching delivery times to as much as 18 months, according to network operator RETN. RETN says that network operators and telcos are now directly competing with AI datacenters for chips and other components. As Reg readers will be aware, memory prices have soared by four or five times over the past year or so, but RETN says optical networking equipment prices have risen by around 50 percent since the start of 2026. Worse are the extended delivery times, with optical network kit that used to arrive within three months now taking 12 to 15, and some orders taking up to 18 months. This is as bad as, if not worse than, the shortages during the pandemic, when chip supply problems left network vendors unable to fulfill orders . The issue now is that because of the AI boom, demand is outpacing supplies. In its report, "AI, Connected," RETN says developers building outside established datacenter hubs may need to involve network carriers two to five years before opening. The sudden demand for network kit from hyperscalers and AI campuses is only one factor, RETN says. Raw material shortages, skilled labor shortages, energy constraints, geopolitical tensions, and logistical challenges are also compounding the issue. However, it concedes that many carriers didn't help themselves by previously postponing network upgrades to cut expenditure. That work has now become unavoidable at the worst possible time. Network diversity is now seen as a must-have, the report says. Where customers were once satisfied with two routes to long-haul destinations, they expect operators to provide four or more redundant routes now. The aim is to prevent a single failure from taking down critical services. Multiple connections are only useful protection if they avoid shared physical failure points, such as the same ducts or cable routes. A diverse circuit might cost €1,800 ($1,975) a month instead of €600 ($658), it claims, but an outage could prove far more costly. RETN also says AI datacenters are moving away from populated areas to remote locations, where access to suitable land, power and water may be easier to come by. Hyperscalers are building in the Nordics, where land is affordable, the climate is cooler, and plenty of renewable energy is available. Remote sites may lack the fiber infrastructure needed to connect them to other datacenters and customers. The Register reported on this issue earlier this year. For sites close to cities, developers often fund the fiber themselves, which adds just a few percent to the total project cost. But over longer distances, the case becomes harder to make, and carriers are understandably reluctant to build a long-haul route to serve a single remote site. "We are working closely with the National Cyber Security Centre and Government Cyber Coordination Centre (GC3) to investigate and to bring services back online as quickly as possible and to minimize any disruption. "Regular benefit and pension payments are not affected and will be paid as normal. If an online service you need is unavailable, please try again later. As always, we will never message you to ask for bank details or ask you to click on links." The Register contacted both the DWP and NCSC for more information. The DWP declined to comment beyond the statement issued publicly. GC3 coordinates responses to incidents affecting government. The Government Cyber Unit leads the wider Government Cyber Action Plan, backed by more than £210 million. It is led by the government CISO, Bella Powell. Officials have not commented on any of the usual details one would expect from a cyber incident disclosure, including the specific services that were downed, when they are expected to return, or whether any data is thought to be compromised, even at this early stage. The UK government has also been criticized recently for investing heavily in AI cyber defenses, while the issue of legacy and aging IT continues to be neglected in the background. It announced at the end of October that it was throwing £130 million at AI cyber defense technology , as part of a wider £600 million cross-government AI spending spree announced by the Treasury. technology.title: Royal Navy orders £142M in minehunting drones from US supplier
technology.description: Britain's Royal Navy is investing £142 million ($185 million) in underwater drones to tackle sea mines, but the contract has gone to an American defense supplier. The Ministry of Defence (MoD) says that the UK's ability to protect vital sea routes will be strengthened through the procurement of these Uncrewed Underwater Vehicles (UUVs). These will form part of the Royal Navy's move toward a " Hybrid Navy " comprising a mix of crewed, uncrewed, and autonomous platforms in order to meet future challenges. The UUV selected for the job is the REMUS 620 , built by Huntington Ingalls Industries (HII), the largest military shipbuilding company in the United States. HII has a facility at Portchester, on the south coast of England, but is still a US-owned company. We asked the MoD how the award fits its pledge to prioritize buying British wherever possible, and what share of the contract's value will support UK industry. The contract includes HII's Sea Launcher automated launch and recovery systems and will bring support services previously delivered overseas to the UK. HII says it will support 15 jobs, while the MoD identifies Portchester among the locations benefiting. HII says this is the largest international order in its 25-year history of supplying uncrewed systems. The MoD has previously acquired REMUS 100, REMUS 300, and REMUS 600 vehicles for mine countermeasure operations. The new vehicles will locate sea mines to support clearance operations and help keep shipping routes open. By using drones to comb a body of water for explosive devices, the Royal Navy's crews can be kept a safe distance from any potential immediate threat. Traditionally, this work has been conducted by specialist crewed ships such as the Hunt class or Sandown class , but these are being retired from service in favor of uncrewed systems. The Royal Navy also operates SWEEP , an uncrewed boat towing equipment that mimics a ship's magnetic, acoustic, and electric signatures to trigger mines from a safe distance. The new REMUS underwater vehicles can be sent ahead of other vessels to search beneath the surface, making minehunting operations safer, faster and more flexible, according to the MoD. "This investment strengthens our ability to protect freedom of navigation, which is critical to our security and our economy," said Defence Secretary Wes Streeting MP. Like others in the portfolio, REMUS 620 resembles a naval torpedo. It is capable of operating at depths of 600 meters and has an endurance of up to 110 hours on a single mission. The drones will be integrated with SeeTrack and Neptune software developed by SeeByte in the UK, which is already used by the Royal Navy. In trials announced in October 2025, a REMUS 620 demonstrated launch and recovery using a submerged test fixture replicating a Virginia-class submarine's torpedo tube. The work could enable submarines to deploy and retrieve underwater drones on future missions. ®

"We used to have about 30 PCs, all running slightly different radio shows depending on the time zone where we broadcast," he explained. The PCs were old clunkers running Windows 95 long after Microsoft ended support for the OS. Management knew the machines needed replacing, but funding was probably another year away. "We had to coax them on till then," Bruce wrote. "And by coax, I mean we were buying RAM on eBay because nobody sold the 4MB sticks we needed anymore." Thanks to the tender ministrations of Bruce and his colleagues, the PCs kept humming and the radio stations stayed on the air. Until a lovely spring Tuesday, when Bruce and his crew enjoyed a bucolic cup of tea in the first real sunshine of the season and received a call informing them that one of the stations was down. One of Bruce's mates figured a cranky old PC probably just needed a reboot and headed off to fix it while the rest of the team enjoyed their tea. And then the phone rang again to report another outage, so Bruce and the entire crew went back to work, chatting about which switch or other shared device could have taken out two PCs.
